video_title: Windy shuts down this 'FAKE ARGUMENT' about the LeBron-MJ GOAT debate 🗣️ | First Take

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' legacy goal of winning titles with four different teams
quotes.excerpt: LeBron wants to be the only player in NBA history to win a title with 4 different teams
quotes.quote: There is no doubt LeBron is playing for a different legacy. The legacy being, being the only player in NBA history to win a championship with four different teams. And this is kind of, he is playing on borrowed time. It is like he is playing with some spare change here to be playing in seasons that have never been seen in the NBA, potentially lead a championship, that has to be something in the cap of LeBron James when you think about his legacy.

quotes.speaker: Evan Cohen
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Cohen's ranking of the Knicks and Pacers in the East
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks are number one. They won a championship, I've seen them play together.
quotes.quote: The Knicks are number one. They won a championship, I've seen them play together. Did they lose some pieces? Mitchell Robinson, sure. Andre Drummond coming in to replace him. But that starting five and some of the backups, the role players are all there. The Knicks absolutely are number one. Number two for me, before I even get to the conversation around Philadelphia, I think we have completely overlooked the team in the NBA Finals two years ago. The Indiana Pacers are a Tyrese Haliburton injury away from potentially actually beating the Oklahoma City Thunder, who seemed unbeatable that year in Game 7. They are coming back, Zube is there for Miles Turner, different team, I understand it. They bring in Kelly Oubre off the bench, I like that move. Pascal Siakam, Tyrese Haliburton, that is still a really good team. They have a championship head coach in Rick Carlisle. I know Philadelphia does in Nick Nurse as well, but I like what I've seen over the last few years from Indiana.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst dismisses the LeBron vs Jordan GOAT debate as a fake argument
quotes.excerpt: That's a fake argument. Nobody, nobody would ever give him credit for that.
quotes.quote: I'm totally overruling this. Do you think one person who thinks that Jordan is ahead of LeBron would say, oh, he won four championships with four different teams, oh, he's number one? That's a fake argument. Nobody, nobody would ever give him credit for that. We have had eight different champions in the last eight years, and LeBron went to eight straight finals. Has anybody said, boy, you know what, that getting in eight straight finals is pretty good, that would be pretty good? No, no one has said that because they've already decided. There's nobody that's going to be swayed by anything. They've already decided. They just want to hear your argument so that they can state their argument. That's why the whole thing is ridiculous.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the difficulty of building a superteam in the modern NBA
quotes.excerpt: History tells us that no matter what, a brand new superteam doesn't get to the top
quotes.quote: In the superteam era, which we're going to go back to the Celtics who started this, the only team that's ever climbed to the top in the first year was those Celtics. They had multiple seven-game series just to get out of the Eastern Conference. It was very difficult for them and then they were at the top for one year. So, history tells us that no matter what, a brand new superteam doesn't get to the top in the first year. But I have to see, and again, the 76ers are going to have to prove that they can win 16 playoff games to me by what they do on the defensive end.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Knicks' critical contract situation with Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.excerpt: I think this is low-key one of the most important things that's going to happen this summer
quotes.quote: I think this is low-key one of the most important things that's going to happen this summer is how the Knicks handle this Karl-Anthony Towns situation. Unlike Steph Curry or Anthony Davis or some other guys, his extension eligible now. They could do this deal today. They haven't done the deal. They don't have an agreement on it. And so, you know, KAT is coming off of the highest achievement in his career, he was awesome in the playoffs. He could look at the Knicks with a straight face and say, I'm a max player, pay me. But in the modern era, you just have to be careful with this situation.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on how the Nuggets' contract situation with Jamal Murray created roster constraints
quotes.excerpt: One of the reasons why the Nuggets are in the situation that they're in right now
quotes.quote: One of the reasons why the Nuggets are in the situation that they're in right now where they're facing a jail is because they paid Jamal Murray a max extension when he probably wasn't a max player. And now it's part of the reason why they're they're handcuffed. The Milwaukee Bucks ran out of time on their team because their team ran out of assets and was too expensive. You need expert handling to keep your window open. That's why we see the Thunder giving away players right now. They're trying to keep that core together.

quotes.speaker: Evan Cohen
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Cohen praises Karl-Anthony Towns' defensive performance against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: What he did defensively against Victor Wembanyama specifically in that NBA Finals blew me away.
quotes.quote: I am a big believer in defense first. Karl-Anthony Towns was never looked at as a defensive player. What he did defensively against Victor Wembanyama specifically in that NBA Finals blew me away. I didn't think that was there. He was phenomenal. And they changed their offense to some extent to run through him as point center, point forward. This is where, as cheesy as it sounds, the power of friendship that they talk about has to be considered because Leon Rose is the president of basketball operations is likely going to say to Karl-Anthony Towns, the more money we give you, the more of a financial commitment we give you, the more likely it is you're one day on another team. Do you want to present a situation where all of you guys can stay together? And the only way that could happen is if each of them take less.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Nuggets' fiscal responsibility and tax situation
quotes.excerpt: Right now, they are looking at a $68 million tax bill for this season.
quotes.quote: In the history of the Nuggets franchise, dating back to 2002 when the luxury tax came into play, the Nuggets have paid about 52 or 53 million in luxury tax total. Their owner, Stan Kroenke, and their governor, Josh Kroenke, they've just been very fiscally responsible. By the way, the Kroenke family has won a Super Bowl, a Stanley Cup, an NBA championship, and they just Arsenal, their Premier League team just won their Premier League title. They know how to operate sports teams, okay? And they are very cautious on spending. Right now, they are looking at a $68 million tax bill for this season. I'm going to say that again. They paid 53 million over the last 23 years, 53. This year they're looking at 68. Do we believe they're actually going to pay 68 million this year? The league is watching, and if they do make a cost-cutting move, how drastic and how severe is it going to be? They've got a big free agent out there, Peyton Watson, we're not sure what they're going to do.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Nikola Jokic's contract extension and the Nuggets' future
quotes.excerpt: Jokic has said multiple times on the record, I'm going to be a Nugget for life.
quotes.quote: When Nikola Jokic says, again, looking with the straight face, I'm not signing a contract extension this summer, but don't worry, I'll sign it next summer, and I'm going to do that so I can get one more year on the back end, I'm not in position to say that that's not true. Jokic has said multiple times on the record, I'm going to be a Nugget for life. But if you are the Nuggets and you're coming off of multiple seasons where you've advanced less and less, and now your salary is forcing you to keep, you know, take the team sort of apart year to year, do you feel ultimate comfort about Jokic signing that extension next year? Maybe they do. Maybe everybody's on the up and up and Jokic doesn't really care if the owners are worried about their tax bill, maybe that's fine. But until Nikola Jokic signs that contract extension, and until the Nuggets prove that they can, they can work within their financial situation and keep this team going, it's going to be one of the big questions hanging over the future of the league.

quotes.speaker: Evan Cohen
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Cohen questions why the same standard isn't applied to Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: Why don't we have that same mentality towards Giannis? Same resume. Not same player.
quotes.quote: Some people could be sitting here listening to Windy and watching us and saying, well, what are you guys doing? You're talking about a championship player and a multiple-time MVP for one franchise in a non-New York, LA, Chicago market, and you think that person is ever going to get moved? Why don't we have that same mentality towards Giannis? Same resume. Not same player. How many times did we sit here and say, Giannis got to get out of there, right? He's a one-time champion, a multiple-time MVP. Just like Jokic. And we had all of this energy towards they have to move on from Giannis, Giannis has to move on from them. I would argue that what Milwaukee tried to do since winning a championship for Giannis was way greater than what Denver has tried to do for Jokic since winning a championship. The difference is, it didn't work in Milwaukee, but it's not working running it back over and over again in Denver. I am not suggesting that he's ever going to play another game for another team. What I am saying is, we have chosen to treat him differently than we chose Giannis when in essence, they have a very similar, if not the same resume.
